english.note: Use 嚇親 as the everyday all-purpose verb when something suddenly frightens or alarms someone.
This is the all-purpose everyday choice for making someone suddenly feel scared or startled.
Use 嚇親 as the all-purpose spoken choice when something frightens or emotionally shocks someone.
This is the all-purpose choice when an action or event frightens or startles someone.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for causing someone to feel frightened or horrified.
Use 嚇親 as the all-purpose verb for suddenly frightening someone or being startled.
Use 嚇親 as the all-purpose colloquial choice when dismay means causing fear or alarm.
Use this as the all-purpose everyday choice when something alarms or upsets someone.
Use this for frightening or startling someone, especially when the result is not necessarily prolonged panic.
Use this when a sudden event makes someone involuntarily flinch or become startled.

examples.english: That loud bang did alarm me.
examples.traditional: 頭先嗰聲巨響嚇親我喇。
